contradictions.what: Rep says nothing got silence and it was a good cycle, yet no customer-specific value figure reached the CFO and the business-case request went unmet.
Rep says IT was fine with it, later says IT lead was nervous about moving before spring and conditional on finance.
Rep says the rate killed it and more rate room would win, but also concedes the CFO saw a same-rate page with no cost-of-failure value, suggesting a value gap.
Martin's quote is relayed in two different wordings; both are secondhand via Lucy.
Lucy called approval a formality right before the CFO meeting, then reported rejection.
Rep says 'same thing' is untrue, yet did not provide the data that would have shown the difference.

dodges.question: Which part of our pitch got a reaction, and which got silence?
dodges.what: Answered 'Silence, honestly, nothing bombed', then later revealed no customer-specific value and unmet business-case request.

dodges.question: Did we put a figure on the value they'd get? A figure for Fernbrook.
dodges.what: First answered with the generic uplift slide; only admitted no Fernbrook figure after the follow-up.

dodges.question: So what did Martin have in front of him about what one in twelve orders was costing?
dodges.what: Answered 'Nothing from us. I assume Lucy told him.' after a pause.

dodges.question: What did they ask for that we couldn't show?
dodges.what: Answered by saying he sent the deck and pricing, not addressing that the business case could not be shown.
